sections.html:
Kansas's biggest city, Wichita, is also the Sedgwick County seat. It had 397,532 residents in 2020 and an estimated 400,987 in 2025, spread over about 166.5 square miles. One county office values every house, and one treasurer bills it, whether it is in Old Town, Delano or a newer subdivision.

The Appraiser sets values and the Treasurer collects. The city has no tax office of its own.

Tax statements arrive every November. Pay half or the whole bill by December 20. The other half comes due May 10 of the following year.

  • Cards work online, by phone at 1-833-303-6683, or in person at the Ruffin Building, 100 N. Broadway, Suite 100.
  • You may pay in part, except on a parcel already picked for a tax foreclosure sale.
  • A written application can set up monthly prepayments, at least $20 a month for 10 months, and the Treasurer approves or denies each one.
  • The only official relief program for seniors or low-income owners is the state Homestead program, reached at 1-785-368-8222.

You can also sign up for a payment reminder from the Treasurer. If you are closing in the fall, ask the title company whether the November bill has posted yet, because it changes the payoff.

sections.h2: How a Wichita tax bill is calculated
sections.html:
Start with the appraised value, take 11.5% of it for a house, and apply the combined mill levy to that. A mill equals $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value. A typical Wichita taxpayer's fiscal year 2025 levy splits like this:

Taxing bodyMillsShare of bill
USD 259 (Wichita schools)51.38744.9%
City of Wichita32.81628.7%
Sedgwick County28.70125.1%
State of Kansas1.5001.3%

The city's own Mill Levy Facts sheet estimates 32.340 mills for the 2026 budget year, split between the general fund (25.505) and debt service (6.835). The same sheet lists other assessment rates: 25% for commercial property and 12% for vacant lots.

The school share is the largest piece. When a buyer asks what the taxes will be, the answer depends on the school district and any special assessments, so a quick look at the parcel record beats a guess.

Specials pay for neighborhood improvements like streets, sewers and sidewalks. Unless the owner prepaid, they ride along on the property tax bill for 10 to 15 years.

What is left on a special becomes part of your payoff at sale. A house on a freshly improved street may add a real amount to each half-year bill. Find the specials line on your statement before naming a price or weighing offers.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Wichita valuation
sections.html:
Each tax year allows a single appeal, and it starts with the informal step.

  1. Notices of value go in the mail March 1.
  2. The appeal form on the back of the notice must be returned within 30 days, normally by March 31.
  3. An interview notice arrives about 10 days before you talk with the appraiser, by phone or face to face.
  4. A letter then reports whether your value changed.
  5. Still unhappy? The Board of Tax Appeals small claims division hears single-family homes and non-agricultural property valued under $3 million, and you must file within 30 days of the mailed result. Filing fees may apply.

Missed March? A Payment Under Protest is your second chance. File the form with your December 20 or May 10 payment, or by January 31 when a mortgage company pays. Strong evidence includes comparable sales, a recent private appraisal, a purchase contract, dated photos and signed repair estimates. Get documents in at least three business days before your appointment.

Hail and straight-line wind keep coming back in Wichita, and roofs suffer first. With unrepaired storm damage you can claim insurance and fix it before listing, list with a repair credit or lower price, or sell as-is to a buyer who factors the repairs into the offer.

Signed repair estimates and dated damage photos also count as evidence in a value appeal, and a lower value means a lower tax bill.

sections.h2: What happens if Wichita property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Late payments accrue interest, and years of delinquency can end at a county auction. The real property interest rate is 13% for 2026, built from the state rate in K.S.A. 79-2968 plus five percentage points.

K.S.A. 79-2801 requires counties to foreclose on delinquent tax liens and sell the property. Sedgwick County chooses parcels that are two and a half or three and a half years behind. After the District Court case is filed, getting the parcel back takes cash or certified funds covering every delinquent year, with interest and fees. An auction buyer does not owe the old taxes, and the former owner loses all claim.

A parcel 3 1/2 years behind can be sold, and there is usually one sale a year. The Treasurer's tax foreclosure page posts case information for the next auction. For a balance, call (316) 660-9000.

sections.h2: Selling a Wichita house that owes back taxes
sections.html:
Yes, it can be done. The title company closes the sale and pays back tax out of the proceeds, as it would any lien. Order of events is what counts: a parcel already in a foreclosure case needs the full balance in certified funds to come out, so the sale must have a firm closing date.

Steps that usually help:

  • Find the parcel record and write down unpaid years, interest and specials.
  • See whether the parcel is on the Treasurer's delinquent or foreclosure list.
  • Get a payoff from the title company good through your expected closing date.
  • Weigh whether a value appeal is worth the effort before you close.

Cash Home Buyers can look at an as-is Wichita house with tax due and give you a written offer to compare.

When a Wichita house sells, the current year's tax is usually split by the days each side owns the house. If the November bill has not posted yet, the title company estimates the amount and holds it back, so ask early how they plan to handle it. Any unpaid half from a prior due date should be cleared first, since interest keeps building until it is paid.

sections.h2: What to have ready before closing
sections.html: Have the newest tax statement, the valuation notice, any specials schedule and a photo ID on hand. With a mortgage open, ask the lender for a payoff figure. The title company divides this year's bill with the buyer and deducts any back balance from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Is Wichita property tax paid to the city or the county?
faqs.a: The county does. One Treasurer statement covers Sedgwick County, the City of Wichita, USD 259 and the state, using the value the Appraiser set.

faqs.q: What is the Wichita residential assessment rate?
faqs.a: A house is assessed at 11.5% of appraised value, and the combined mill levy applies to that figure.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Wichita valuation?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the notice mailing, usually March 31, for the informal form. Later, a Payment Under Protest goes in with the December 20 or May 10 payment, or by January 31 if a lender pays.

faqs.q: How long can taxes go unpaid before Sedgwick County sells a house?
faqs.a: A parcel 3 1/2 years delinquent can be auctioned, and warning notices name properties two and a half or three and a half years behind. After filing, the owner needs cash or certified funds for every delinquent year.

faqs.q: Does a special assessment affect what I net when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Unless prepaid, specials for streets, sewers or sidewalks stay on the tax bill for 10 to 15 years, so look up the balance before comparing offers.
